text: Before Dmitri builds anything, this lesson designs the Warranty Claim table itself -- seven fields, and one relationship that matters more than the rest.
partner_company, equipment_serial, issue_description, state, labor_hours, parts_cost, resolution_notes -- six are straightforward, state included.
partner_company points at the same Company table Brindlewood already uses for every partner -- the same table a partner's own login already points to.
That shared reference is what makes 'whose claim is this' answerable later. The ACL itself, and the real table, come in lessons still ahead.
Next: planning exactly how that comparison gets enforced -- and everywhere it has to hold.
